name: Spreadsheets and Data
tagline: Right formulas, clean data and clear analysis in Excel and Google Sheets
description: Walks your AI through a method for solving real spreadsheet problems in Excel and Google Sheets: it confirms your version and language, diagnoses the structure and the data types, picks the simplest solution (XLOOKUP, INDEX with MATCH, SUMIFS, a PivotTable, FILTER or QUERY) and writes the formula in your spreadsheet's language, English or Brazilian Portuguese, with the right argument separator, together with a test script for you to check it. The knowledge base covers function names, lookups, data cleaning and dates, QUERY and limits, with source and date. It does not access your spreadsheet or run formulas: you apply and test them. It also does not write macros unless you insist.

creator.bio: Senior software engineer with 12 years in React and Node.js. Was a platform tech lead at a fintech and writes about accessibility and testing.

questions.ask: Which program do you use for spreadsheets?
questions.why: Functions such as XLOOKUP, FILTER and QUERY depend on the program and the version; I only write what works in yours.

questions.ask: Is your spreadsheet in English or in Portuguese?
questions.why: It sets the function names and whether the separator is a comma or a semicolon.

questions.ask: How would you describe your level with formulas?
questions.why: It adjusts how much I explain about each argument and whether I use helper columns instead of long formulas.

questions.ask: What do you mostly use spreadsheets for?
questions.why: I pick examples and precautions from your day to day, such as sales, inventory or reports.

beforeAfter.prompt: My VLOOKUP returns #N/A even though the code exists in the other sheet.
beforeAfter.withoutSolver: Check that the lookup value exists in the first column of the range and use =VLOOKUP(A2,Sheet2!A:B,2,FALSE).
beforeAfter.withSolver: Asks for your version and language, has you test =ISTEXT(A2) in both sheets and =LEN(A2) to spot text against number or a stray space, and delivers the fix in your spreadsheet's language: =XLOOKUP(VALUE(TRIM(A2)),Sheet2!A2:A500,Sheet2!B2:B500,"not found") in Excel 365 or 2021, and INDEX with MATCH in Excel 2019. Ends with a three-row test script.

beforeAfter.prompt: I want the total sales by salesperson and by month in a Google spreadsheet.
beforeAfter.withoutSolver: You can use SUMIF to add up each salesperson's sales.
beforeAfter.withSolver: Checks that the data is tabular and that the Date column holds real dates, then delivers =QUERY(A1:C,"select B, sum(C) where A is not null group by B pivot month(A)+1",1), explaining that month() starts at zero, hence the +1, with a no-formula PivotTable alternative.

beforeAfter.prompt: My imported dates are left-aligned and the filter does not group by month.
beforeAfter.withoutSolver: Format the column as a date.
beforeAfter.withSolver: Explains that they are text and that formatting does not convert them, tests the conversion with a day greater than 12 so day and month do not get swapped, writes =DATEVALUE(A2) or, if the format is fixed, =DATE(RIGHT(A2,4),MID(A2,4,2),LEFT(A2,2)), and tells you to apply it on a copy and check the row count and the sum before pasting values.

versions.notes: Guide to lookup formulas and data cleaning.
Adds QUERY in Google Sheets, PivotTables and recipes for dates stored as text.

Method rewritten in 4 steps (understand, prepare the data, choose the solution, test and deliver). Knowledge base reorganized into 7 files with source and date: Portuguese function names checked against Microsoft's pages, availability by Excel version, limits, QUERY and privacy. Fix: the shortcut to create a Table is Ctrl+T (the previous text said Ctrl+Alt+T). Three ready-made templates and calibration saved in the specialist's memory. Twelve or more evaluation cases; the earlier scores were withdrawn because they did not match existing cases.
